newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin stays in hospital for further tests.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin stays in hospital for further tests.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, undergoing a series of medical tests at Russia's Central Clinical Hospital, will spend another two days as an in-patient there, the presidential press office said on Monday.
It gave no details of what tests would be carried out.
Spokesmen said on Saturday the hospital tests would help prepare the ground for Yeltsin's planned heart operation, but they did not say how long he would stay in hospital.

Yeltsin, 65, broke a long Kremlin tradition of secrecy about the health of Moscow's leaders earlier this month when he said he was going to have an operation on his heart. The alternative, the president told reporters, was to have a sedentary life.
He went into hospital for the tests last Friday.

Yeltsin, who had two heart attacks last year, disappeared between the two rounds of Russia's presidential election, prompting speculation that he had been taken ill. He has been on holiday outside Moscow for over a week.
He agreed earlier this month to have a heart bypass to improve blood supply to the heart, and doctors will decide later this month exactly when to operate.
Bypass surgery is much more common in the United States and other Western countries than in Russia.
The Kremlin has invited experienced Western cardiologists to join the team of consultants.
Yeltsin has said he will have the operation in Russia rather than travelling abroad for treatment.
His absence has prompted speculation about who would take the reins during the surgery and who would hold the "red button" triggering Russia's nuclear arsenal.
NTV commercial television said on Sunday Yeltsin may hand over Russia's "nuclear button" to his prime minister only for as long as he is unconscious.
